w: An 8-kilometre tidal island across the mouth of Tasman Bay, Rabbit Island shows evidence of Maori occupation over 800 years and became a public reserve in 1908. A causeway crosses the tidal flats to a long, safe swimming beach backed by pine-topped dunes, and the Great Taste Trail runs through it.
s: Tidal island beach reached by causeway near Nelson
_facts: 8 km long, 15 sq km tidal island on the southern edge of Tasman Bay
Evidence of Maori occupation for over 800 years; became a public reserve in 1908
Popular swimming beach reached by causeway, backed by pine-covered sand dunes
Part of the Great Taste Trail cycle route between Richmond and Motueka

w: Standing at 1 Trafalgar Square as seat of the Bishop of Nelson, Christ Church Cathedral was completed in a Modernist Gothic Revival style: 58 metres long, 27 metres wide, with a 35-metre tower over the square. It seats 350 as the mother church of the Anglican Diocese of Nelson.
s: Modernist Gothic cathedral seating 350 in Trafalgar Square
_facts: Anglican cathedral at 1 Trafalgar Square, Nelson; seat of the Bishop of Nelson
Mother church of the Diocese of Nelson
Modernist Gothic Revival style: 58m long, 27m wide, 35m tower

w: Near Ernest Rutherford's birthplace in Brightwater, a statue by Monaco sculptor Paul Walshe depicts the future Nobel laureate as a child. Surrounding terraces are planted with trees from Canada, England and New Zealand, the countries where he worked, and the memorial opened in 1991.
s: Child statue of the Nobel physicist, near his birthplace
_facts: Statue of Ernest Rutherford, 1908 Nobel Prize in Chemistry winner, depicted as a child
Located near his birthplace in Brightwater, New Zealand
Sculpted by Paul Walshe of Monaco
Terraced mound planted with trees from Canada, England and New Zealand; cost $400,000, opened 1991

w: St Michael's Church in Waimea West dates to 1843, when it became the first church building erected in Nelson Province. Its parish has held continuous services longer than any other in New Zealand, and the building is registered category 1 by Heritage New Zealand.
_facts: Historic Anglican church in Waimea West, built 1843
First church building in Nelson Province
Oldest parish with continuous services in New Zealand
Registered category 1 by Heritage New Zealand
